docRequirement: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/whats-new/2026-w20.md line 91 (last cell of the `digest-wins-grid`, under `Other wins`): "Agent tool `subagent_type` now matches case- and separator-insensitively, so `"Code Reviewer"` resolves to `code-reviewer`". A requested subagent type must therefore resolve to a defined agent whenever it differs from that agent's name only in letter case AND/OR in separator characters (space, hyphen, underscore). Case-insensitivity alone does not satisfy the sentence: the page's own worked example ("Code Reviewer" -> code-reviewer) differs by a separator, not by case.
current: Case- and trim-insensitive only; separator-insensitive nowhere. `normalizeName` is the single normalizer for agent names and is `name.trim().toLowerCase()` with no separator folding (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:281-283). `resolveAgentDefinition` normalises the request through it and then does two EXACT comparisons — `defs.find(def => def.name === normalized)` then `defs.find(def => def.aliases?.includes(normalized))` — throwing `Unknown agent "<name>". Available agents: ...` when both miss (definitions.ts:718-731, throw at :728). Both comparison arms share the gap because the stored side is normalised by the same function: markdown/JSON definitions at definitions.ts:441, host-supplied runtime definitions at :688-:690, author-declared aliases at :699. MEASURED on this rig against a workspace holding `code-reviewer.md` (bun, real module, no mocks): "code-reviewer" -> OK, "CODE-REVIEWER" -> OK, " Code-Reviewer " -> OK (two positive controls: case folding and trimming really are live), "Code Reviewer" -> THROW Unknown agent, "code_reviewer" -> THROW Unknown agent, "codereviewer" -> THROW Unknown agent. Second, symmetric arm, also measured: a definition declaring `name: Code Reviewer Two` is STORED as `"code reviewer two"` (definitions.ts:441 lowercases but keeps the space), so it resolves only from that exact spaced spelling and throws for `code-reviewer-two` — the kebab spelling a model naturally emits. Nothing upstream compensates: the model's string reaches the resolver raw — `asTask` only type-checks `typeof value.agent !== 'string'` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.ts:101-114), `normalizeSubagentRequest` never touches the value (:122-160), and it is passed straight in at :512; the advertised parameter schema is a bare `agent: { type: 'string' }` with no enum of live agent names (:382, :419, :432). The workflow path is identical (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/workflow-tool.ts:590). One layer ABOVE the resolver the same case-only fold repeats and fails harder: the invoked-skill agent ceiling stores its allow-set as `agents.map(agent => agent.toLowerCase())` (packages/shared/src/agent/core/prerequisite-manager.ts:213) and collects the model's `agent`/`subagent_type` values as `.trim().toLowerCase()` (:448-452), rejecting a mismatch at :461 with `Tool "..." requested an agent outside the invoked skill agent ceiling.` — a message that does NOT enumerate the available agents. The separator-insensitive normaliser this repo already owns sits in a SIBLING subsystem and is not shared: `parsePermissionMode` does `mode.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[-_ ]/g, '')` and its doc comment literally says "case- and separator-insensitively" (packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts:238-244).
divergence: Exactly one half of a two-part rule is missing: case (and trim) folding is implemented, separator folding is not. No key name, value, schema or wire field is wrong — the shapes are right and the fix is a comparison change, not a rename. The gap is symmetric across both comparison arms (requested name and stored name/aliases run through the same `normalizeName`), so it bites in two directions: a hyphen/underscore/space variant of a correctly-named agent is rejected, and an agent whose declared name contains a space is stored with that space and is unreachable by its kebab spelling. Consequence, stated accurately (the original finding overstated it as "the same class as the Task->Agent rename that broke every turn"): the call is REJECTED with a retryable tool error that enumerates the available agents, so the model can recover on the next tool call — not a broken turn. The one place it degrades further is under an active invoked-skill agent ceiling, where prerequisite-manager.ts:461 rejects first with a message carrying no agent list.

change.what: Add, next to `normalizeName` (:281-283), `function foldAgentName(name: string): string { return name.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/[-_\s]+/g, ''); }` — the same fold `parsePermissionMode` already uses (agent/mode-types.ts:242), widened from `[-_ ]` to `\s` so a tab folds too. In `resolveAgentDefinition`, compute `const folded = foldAgentName(name);` and APPEND two fallbacks after the existing exact lookups at :725-726, keeping exact-first ordering so no name that resolves today changes target: `?? defs.find(def => foldAgentName(def.name) === folded) ?? defs.find(def => def.aliases?.some(alias => foldAgentName(alias) === folded))`. Roughly four added lines. Two things must NOT change in this edit: (1) leave the reserved-fork short-circuit at :723 on `normalizeName` — folding it would let `for_k`/`f-o-r-k` claim the reserved fork type while `setUnlessReserved` (:666-669, via `isForkAgentName` :234-236) still blocks only the exact spelling, i.e. a shadowing widening; (2) do NOT fold `normalizeName` itself, nor the stored `name` at :441 / :688-:690 / :699 — those strings are `Map` keys at :653/:668/:702 and travel the host->Pi descriptor, so folding them silently collapses `code-reviewer` and `code_reviewer` into one entry (last writer wins) and moves a wire value.
Export `foldAgentName` alongside it so the skill-ceiling fold reuses the one folder instead of copying the regex. One line.

Replace the case-only folds with `foldAgentName` on BOTH sides so the ceiling agrees with the resolver: at :213 build the set as `new Set(agents.map(foldAgentName))`, and at :452 store `requested.add(foldAgentName(record[key] as string))`; the membership test at :461 then compares folded to folded. Leave the hardcoded `'review' | 'reviewer' | 'guardian'` branch at :438-442 alone (no separators involved). Without this edit the resolver fix is invisible whenever an invoked skill declares an `agent:` restriction, because :461 rejects the doc's spelling before the resolver ever runs.

Add the doc's own example as a positive: with a workspace `code-reviewer.md` loaded, `resolveAgentDefinition('Code Reviewer')` and `resolveAgentDefinition('code_reviewer')` both return `code-reviewer`. Add two negatives/boundaries: an unrelated name still throws `Unknown agent`, and when both `code-reviewer` and `codereviewer` are defined each exact spelling still resolves to itself (exact-before-folded ordering). Existing expectations survive unchanged — `Unknown agent "filesystem-only"` (definitions.test.ts:422) and `"architect"` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/agent-defs.test.ts:19) both still miss under folding.

Tests that exercise the resolver: packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.test.ts, packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/agent-defs.test.ts, packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.fork-subagent.test.ts. WIRE/PERSISTENCE: as scoped this fix touches NO wire or persisted value — the host->Pi agent descriptor (`PiRuntimeAgentDefinitionDescriptor`, packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:640-665, `schemaVersion: 2`, `key`/`name`, `sha256`/`definitionDigest`, parsed back at :300-360) keeps its current `key`/`name`, and the raw requested string keeps being recorded as `agentType: task.agent` in the orchestration progress payload (subagent-tool.ts:495) and in the workflow journal replay keys. That immunity depends on the fix staying a comparison-only fold: changing `normalizeName`/:441/:688 instead WOULD move a wire value and a Map key, which is this repo's risk trigger. Sibling exact-match sites deliberately left out of scope, because they resolve AUTHOR-declared references rather than `subagent_type`: `resolveReferences` (runtime-agent-definition.ts:215-228, case-SENSITIVE match on `key`/`logicalName`) and packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2557 (`invocation.restrictions.agent` vs `candidate.key` / `candidate.name`) — folding those is a separate decision, and naming them here so a later sweep does not read them as part of this row. On the Claude backend the SDK's own native binary owns `subagent_type` resolution; packages/ui/src/components/chat/TurnCard.tsx:1259 only reads `toolInput.subagent_type` for display.
userImpact: Concrete but low-grade and self-healing. When the Pi orchestrator's `subagent`/`workflow` tool is called with an agent name that differs from the definition only by a separator — "Code Reviewer" or "code_reviewer" for `code-reviewer`, which is exactly the case Claude's page says now works — the user sees a FAILED tool call in the turn card reading `Unknown agent "Code Reviewer". Available agents: scout, planner, worker, reviewer, ...`, then a retry on the next tool call: one wasted round trip and a red step in the transcript, not a broken turn. Two situations make it worse rather than latent. (1) A user- or plugin-authored agent whose frontmatter `name` carries a space (`name: Code Reviewer`) is stored as `"code reviewer"` and is in practice unaddressable, because the model reliably emits the kebab form — that agent simply never runs (MEASURED). (2) When an invoked skill declares an `agent:` restriction, the invoked-skill ceiling rejects the same spelling one layer earlier with `Tool "subagent" requested an agent outside the invoked skill agent ceiling.`, which lists no agents, so the model has nothing to correct against and can loop or abandon the delegation.
